title: Georgia's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Georgia's 2nd Congressional District features 17-term Democratic incumbent Rep. Sanford Bishop facing Republican businessman Matt Day and Communist Party candidate Brandon Daley. Bishop, a moderate Blue Dog Democrat who has held the seat since 1993, ran unopposed in the Democratic primary, while Day won the Republican primary uncontested. The district covers a largely rural and agricultural region of southwest Georgia including Albany, Americus, and parts of Macon and Columbus. The Cook Political Report rates the race as Solidly Democratic, though ongoing redistricting debates could reshape the district's boundaries for future cycles.

candidates.name: Sanford Bishop
candidates.summary: Sanford Dixon Bishop Jr. is an American lawyer and politician serving as the U.S. representative for Georgia's 2nd congressional district since 1993, making him the dean of Georgia's congressional delegation. He is a member of the Blue Dog Coalition, a group of moderate to conservative House Democrats, and serves as Ranking Member on the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture. Bishop previously served in the Georgia House of Representatives (1977-1991) and the Georgia State Senate (1991-1993), and has consistently won re-election by comfortable margins in recent cycles.

candidates.name: Matt Day
candidates.summary: Benjamin Matthew Day is a businessman and Republican candidate for U.S. House in Georgia's 2nd Congressional District. He is the founder of multiple companies in the construction and manufacturing staffing sectors, including Glaziers on Demand (2013), Glazier Nation (2019), and ChoreNab (2025). Day describes himself as a commonsense conservative and says his mission is to fight corruption, government waste, and the size of government.
